page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The instance provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU based on the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a 36 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration supporting AES instructions. Memory is provisioned at 2.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, relying on external network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark testing highlights the performance characteristics of its single-core Neoverse-V2 design. In single-threaded compression tests, bzip3 decompression reached 14.2 GB/sec, placing in the top 25 percent of tested systems, while gzip single-threaded compression achieved an average 30.02 GB/sec. Stress-ng single-core execution scored 1694.9, aligning with the median tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded aggregate throughput remains constrained by the single-vCPU ceiling. Memory bandwidth benchmarks recorded 30.42 GB/sec for large-block reads and 12.18 GB/sec for large-block writes, while Redis SET performance reached 2.25 million operations per second and static web serving achieved 2.51 GB/sec.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the c8gb.medium provides a modern ARMv9 execution environment in an entry-level footprint, avoiding multi-tenant CPU contention via dedicated core scheduling. The lack of local NVMe storage and the 2.0 GB memory boundary make it unsuitable for high-throughput databases, in-memory caching fleets, or large compilation tasks. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, task workers, single-threaded batch processing, edge logic, and low-traffic web endpoints.
